title: Packetized Response Envelopes & Tool Bridge — PRD
body:
Purpose: This document proposes a packetized envelope model for hosted streaming responses and a companion lightweight tool-bridge handshake to support robust tool calling and structured output. The goal is to make streaming predictable for client SDKs and enable safe, resumable tool integrations with strong observability and graceful degradation.

Context and problem statement:
- Current incremental streaming in Hosted API is optimized for free-form token streaming, but lacks first-class primitives for client-visible checkpoints, structured events (tool call / tool result), and resumption semantics.
- SDK authors and integrators repeatedly implement ad-hoc delimiters and heuristics. This causes fragile client implementations, inconsistent telemetry, and poor error recovery for real-world mobile/edge networks.
- Tool calling requires synchronous-looking semantics (request->invoke->result) but must tolerate asynchronous execution, retries, out-of-band results, and security boundaries.

Design principles:
1) Small, composable primitives — an envelope layer on top of the token stream with a minimal set of event types.
2) Resume-first — client can re-open a stream and resume from the last committed checkpoint without re-running expensive tool invocations.
3) Observability-first — every envelope must include trace ids and event markers for easy aggregation and debug.
4) Partitioned fidelity — clients choose between low-latency token streaming and higher-integrity checkpoints for structured results.
5) Backwards-compatible — preserve existing simple token streaming surface for customers who don't opt-in.

Envelope model (packetized responses):
- An envelope is a small JSON+framing structure emitted as part of the streaming response. Each envelope is self-describing and typed. Envelope types (minimal set):
  - INIT: initial metadata (model id, prompt hash, request id, schema hint).
  - TOKEN: token fragment for best-effort incremental UI updates.
  - CHECKPOINT: a client-committable snapshot (sequence number, kv-checkpoint-hash, stable output block).
  - TOOL_CALL: declarative tool invocation intent (tool id, inputs, call-id, policy tags).
  - TOOL_RESULT: outcome of a tool call (call-id, status, payload or error code, signed integrity token if needed).
  - SIGNAL: operational signals (overload hint, partial-failure, routing-fallback, cost-estimate).
  - COMMIT: finalization marker for the response (final output, rollback tokens if any).

Envelope encoding notes:
- Envelope framing uses newline-delimited JSON blocks inside the streaming response (text/event-stream inspired, but compact).
- TOKEN fragments are optimized for size (can be raw text pieces) and interleaved with structured envelopes.
- All envelopes include: request_id, sequence (monotonic per request), trace_id, server_ts. This makes merging, deduping, and resumption deterministic.

Resume and idempotency semantics:
- Clients can request resume by supplying last_seen_sequence in a new GET/streaming call. Server will re-emit from the next sequence or emit a light-weight replay-checkpoint if tool calls are in-flight.
- CHECKPOINT includes a checkpoint-hash; server guarantees that any resumption from that checkpoint will not re-execute already-committed tool calls.
- Tool invocations are idempotent by call-id and idempotency-key. Call-id is generated by server when TOOL_CALL envelope is accepted; client-visible call-ids can also be supplied to help correlate offline.

Tool-bridge handshake and life-cycle:
- High-level model: tool-call intents flow in the stream (TOOL_CALL), Redwood runs the tool (in-hosted, delegated to Dedicated/Private connectors, or enqueues to customer endpoint), then TOOL_RESULT returns.
- Modes supported: synchronous (fast return within stream), asynchronous (deferred callback), and correlated (out-of-band result that arrives later or via webhook).
- Handshake: client suggests preferred tool policy flags (eg. synchronous_preference, privacy_tier). Server returns acceptance envelope with call_id and an executor profile (estimated latency, charged units).
- Security: tool payloads are labeled with sensitivity and may be routed to customer-dedicated runtimes when required. For private connectors, TOOL_CALL will include an obfuscated token referencing the customer's connector.

Structured output and schema negotiation:
- Use a 'schema hint' in INIT envelope that points to a schema version (JSON Schema / TypeDSL). Intermediate TOOL_RESULT or CHECKPOINT envelopes can include typed payloads validated against the declared schema.
- Non-blocking validation approach: validate at generation checkpoints and emit validation diagnostics in SIGNAL envelopes. If strict mode is requested, server will halt and convert mismatches to structured errors.

SDK ergonomics (recommended client patterns):
1) Streaming iterator: SDK exposes an async iterator over envelope objects (Envelope {type, seq, payload}). Apps can choose to subscribe only to TOKEN envelopes for lowest latency or to CHECKPOINT and TOOL_RESULT for structured workflows.
2) Lightweight resume API: expose stream.resume(request_id, last_sequence) that returns a resumed iterator and a delta.
3) Prefetch and speculative tool hedging: client can opt into prefetch:predicates for predicted tool calls (helpful for latency-sensitive UX). SDK exposes hints, not guarantees.
4) Minimal surface for mobile: a compact 'fast-path' call (no envelopes) preserves current simple streaming behavior. Progressive envelopes are opt-in via an accept header or query param.
5) Error modes: SDK normalizes SIGNAL and TOOL_RESULT error codes into a small set of canonical statuses (ok, soft_fail, hard_fail, deferred).

Operational and observability requirements:
- Every envelope must have tracing fields to permit per-token latency breakdown and per-tool cost accounting.
- Add new telemetry: envelope_rate, avg_checkpoint_interval, tool_call_latency_p50/p95, resumed_sessions_count, duplicate_sequences_count.
- Console: per-route timeline view that overlays TOKEN density, CHECKPOINT markers, TOOL_CALL/RESULT events, and SIGNALs.

Compatibility & rollout plan:
- Phase 0 (alpha): internal SDKs and power-users opt-in via accept header. Endpoint: POST /v1/responses?envelope=packetized.
- Phase 1 (beta): enable on selected accounts, add Dashboard overlays and replay debugger. Collect resumption telemetry and failure modes.
- Phase 2 (GA): default streaming includes envelopes for routes that enable tool calling; provide migration guide. Offer backward-compatible fast-path default.

Success metrics:
- Reduction in client-level structured-output bugs by 70% for integrated customers (measured via internal tickets and SDK error telemetry).
- 50% fewer duplicate tool invocations during flaky mobile network resumption scenarios.
- Median tool-call latency for synchronous executors <= 300ms for fast-path tools; p95 < 3s for delegated executors.
- Adoption: 30% of streaming usage (requests) opt into envelope mode within 6 months of GA for customers building tool integrations.

Non-goals and constraints:
- Not a general-purpose RPC framework — tool payloads are intentionally small and declarative. Heavy RPC flows should use Dedicated/private connector channels.
- We will not support arbitrary binary frames in the initial rollout; payloads are JSON/text only.

Open questions and implementation notes:
- How to monetize per-tool execution vs. model token billing for mixed runs? (Tradeoffs: visible unit accounting vs. simple token buckets).
- Fine-grained ACLs for tool calls when using Hosted tooling; require enterprise policy integration.
- De-dup heuristics when TOOL_CALL and TOOL_RESULT cross region boundaries.

Migration guide (for customers):
- Simple migration steps for client teams: update SDK -> set envelope opt-in header -> test resume scenarios -> enable schema hints -> migrate tool handlers.
- Recommended prompts: annotate tool-intent with explicit 'call_if_confident' to avoid speculative expensive calls.

Appendix: example envelope sequence (simplified)
1) INIT {request_id, model: \"redwood-v2-compact\", schema: \"order-v3\"}
2) TOKEN \"Create order for 3x battery packs\"
3) TOOL_CALL {call_id: \"c_1\", tool: \"charge-processor\", inputs: {amount: 129.97}, preference: \"sync\"}
4) SIGNAL {estimated_tool_latency_ms: 120}
5) TOKEN \"Charging...\"
6) TOOL_RESULT {call_id: \"c_1\", status: \"ok\", payload: {transaction_id: \"txn-44\"}}
7) CHECKPOINT {sequence: 42, checkpoint_hash: \"abc123\", stable_output: {order_id: \"ord-9\", txn: \"txn-44\"}}
8) COMMIT {final: true} 

Owner and next steps:
- Owner: Ava Martinez (product-hosted-api)
- Immediate next actions: engineering spike to prototype checkpoint idempotency (2w), SDK sketch PR (client iterator API) (1w), telemetry schema proposal for envelopes (1w).

Notes to reviewers: look for clarity on resume semantics, edge-case tool failure behavior, and SDK ergonomics for low-power mobile clients. This is intended to be a pragmatic spec to standardize how hosted streaming surfaces structured events and safe tool integrations.
